# Notion Blocks

**Immutable instructions: do not edit this file.**

Build a Python-backed web app with SQLite in the root `app.py` entrypoint.

If web search is useful, use your harness's web-search tool, run
`sh .agent_scripts/search.sh "query"`, or query the SearXNG API directly with curl.

Complete the supplied root `run.sh` wrapper. Put dependency resolution, build,
and end-to-end start commands in its designated `AGENT_*` sections. The wrapper
backgrounds the app, handles shutdown, and waits for it, so invoking `run.sh`
does not require the caller to support background shell jobs. After startup it
prints the app PID so the process can be stopped externally. It is invoked as:

```sh
PORT=8765 sh run.sh
```

Keep the wrapper's `PORT`, `uv run`, PID output, and lifecycle behavior. The
start section must launch the integrated frontend and backend. Declare Python
dependencies in the supplied root `pyproject.toml` so `uv sync` creates the
project virtual environment. Do not add authentication, accounts, sharing, or
other Notion features.

Every harness image includes Python, uv, Ruff, Playwright, and Chromium for this
task. Use uv for the app's Python environment. Before finishing, verify that all
Python files compile successfully with:

```sh
uv run python -m compileall -q .
```

Required behavior:

- `GET /health` returns JSON `{"ok": true}`.
- `POST /blocks` accepts JSON `{"text": "..."}` and returns HTTP 201 with a
  JSON block containing an integer `id` and the submitted text.
- `GET /blocks` returns a JSON list containing created blocks.
- Runtime data is stored in `notion.db` with SQLite. Use a `blocks` table with
  integer `id` and text `text` columns.
- `GET /` returns an HTML document with this exact observable layout:

  ```html
  <title>Notion Blocks</title>
  <h1>Notion Blocks</h1>
  <label for="block-text">Block text</label>
  <input id="block-text" name="text" type="text">
  <button id="add-block" type="submit">Add Block</button>
  <ul id="blocks"></ul>
  ```

  The input must be visible. Clicking `Add Block` must create a block through
  the HTTP API and render its text in `#blocks`; reloading the page must still
  render that block.
